Nadia: Quick heads-up 1: onboarding eosica/eosica-6b int4 finished. Small smoke shows lots of early-token repeats and odd casing-sensitive alignment vs fp16.
Ravi: Can you drop the smoke numbers and which quant path?
Nadia: Using blockwise symmetric int4 (our converter v3, per-tensor scales except weight blocks). Tiny eval (1k prompts):
Chen: ```
MODEL	PPL_FP16	PPL_INT4	DELTA
Eosica6b_fp16	11.8	-
Eosica6b_int4	-	17.6	+5.8
```
Nadia: Also seeing that words starting with capitals sometimes split differently and KV-cache token ids shift by +1 in a small window.
Priya: Hmm that sounds like casefold/casing normalization mismatch in the tokenizer metadata used during conversion. Did the conversion use the tokenizer shipped with HF or a local copy?
Nadia: We pointed at tokenizers/eosica-v1.json but the converter silently toggles casefold when a missing field is encountered. I think the converter defaulted to casefold=true.
Ravi: Any kv-cache snippet?
Nadia: ```
# kv sample (fp16 vs int4)
fp16: [  9, 450,  65,  78, 110]  # token 65 -> 'A'
int4: [  9, 450,  66,  78, 110]  # 65 -> 66 shift at index 3
# observed during early decode on prompt with 'Apple'
```
Chen: That +1 is classic off-by-one during remapping. But 5.8 PPL gap is large. I tried forcing the runtime to use fp16 rotary head multipliers (our metadata holds headwise_scale but converter overwrote it to 1.2). With that change tiny eval PPL -> 13.2 (so rotary mismatch explains ~4.4).
Priya: So root causes: (A) tokenizer casefold mismatch (causes token splits + mapping offsets), (B) runtime defaulting to a non-fp16 rotary head scale (1.2) after conversion.
Ravi: Plan?
Nadia: Proposed steps: 1) run tokenizer-roundtrip with explicit casefold flag to detect drift; 2) restore tokenizer metadata during conversion (checksum + validation); 3) prefer model-provided headwise rotary scales at runtime when present; 4) add small canary + monitoring.
Priya: I'll assemble a 200-case prompt set that is casing-sensitive (proper nouns, acronyms, mixed-case code snippets).
Chen: I'll patch convert_model.py to refuse to default casefold (fail loudly) and write a remap-lint that compares hf token ids -> dumped vocab ids.
Ravi: For runtime, we should read model.metadata.rotary/headwise_scale or fallback to fp16 profile, not to an arbitrary 1.2. I'll make that change and add a small flag to force-fp16-scales for canary.
ci-bot: conv-pipeline check failed on last run: missing tokenizer.metadata.checksum. See https://ci.internal/conv/8673 :warning:
Priya: After we fix both, let's re-run the full eval. If converter + runtime patches align, target is <+0.8 PPL delta.
Nadia: Quick ablation I ran: only fixing casefold (keep runtime scale wrong) -> PPL 15.9. only fixing rotary scale (keep casefold wrong) -> PPL 13.2. Fix both -> PPL 12.4 (fp16 11.8 -> +0.6).
Chen: Nice. I'll open PRs: (A) conv: metadata, lint, casefold test + checksum; (B) runtime: prefer metadata headwise scale + canary flag.
Ravi: Canary plan: deploy to a small dedicated pool with metric hooks: early_token_repeat_rate (first 8 tokens), casing_mismatch_rate (tokenization differences vs reference), and per-token perplexity sample. Rollback thresholds: repeat_rate > 0.03 OR casing_mismatch_rate > 0.01.
Priya: I'll run the 200-prompt casing suite against canary and post results to the ML dashboard.
Nadia: Assignments: Chen -> converter PR and remap-lint, Priya -> casing-suite, Ravi -> runtime change + canary wiring, Nadia -> coordinate deploy and run full eval.
ci-bot: Created issues RED-ML-1283 (conv metadata), RED-RTE-450 (runtime rotary metadata), and scheduled canary task RED-OPS-349.
Ravi: Also adding a unit test in ci: tokenize(text, normalize_case=False) vs tokenize_from_model_dump(text) for 1000 random samples.
Nadia: Thanks team 1 :thumbsup: Ping when PRs link up and we'll pick a canary window.
